Maths Explorer · EN · 03

Congruences and last digits

Lesson and method

High school · number theory

Before you begin

Divisibility, powers and Euclidean division.

Ideas and method

a ≡ b (mod m), with m ≥ 2, means that m divides a − b. They have the same remainder upon division by m. For example, −1 ≡ 6 (mod 7).

Congruences are preserved by addition and multiplication, hence by positive integer powers. Work modulo 10 to find a last digit.

A factor cannot always be cancelled: 2 × 1 ≡ 2 × 4 (mod 6), but 1 is not congruent to 4 modulo 6. A factor coprime to the modulus can be cancelled.

Worked example

The last digits of 3¹, 3², 3³, 3⁴ are 3,9,7,1. The cycle repeats because 3⁴ ≡ 1 (mod 10). Since 2026 = 4 × 506 + 2, the last digit of 3²⁰²⁶ is 9.
